Reviewer agent (local, docs-reviewer): CHANGES_REQUESTED

- [block] The sentence for `.pkit/capabilities/visual-communication/checks.md` says nothing about what changed. The commands that write the answers list take the sentence only from the first line of a top-level item, so they read the item `` - `.pkit/capabilities/visual-communication/checks.md`: these findings change: `` as just "these findings change:". The six sub-bullets under it are dropped. You can see this in the body's own "Documentation this change affects" block: item 5 shows "``these findings change:``". So the person who authorises the merge is told nothing about what changed in checks.md. Under the project-management capability's rule that the pull request lists its answers (DEC-055 point 3), that counts as no sentence, and the check that each `updated` document carries a matching sentence fails. **Fix:** put the whole sentence on one line, ``- `.pkit/capabilities/visual-communication/checks.md`: <sentence>``. For example: "a run's key path becomes a location; adds the rows `run-shape`, `run-key`, `run-style`, `runs-unmarked` and `concept-uncoloured`; extends `component-shape` and `unknown-concept` to runs; `unknown-role`/`role-type` now cover the role a run's style chooses; `text-overflow` asks for attention where runs are measured in different ways; `contrast-drawn` is measured per run." The sub-bullets do match the checks.md diff, so the content is right. Only where it sits is wrong.
- [advisory] The generated "Documentation this change affects" block is stamped `head=fc54db8`, not the reviewed head `cdd97f8`. Its README "Still accurate" reason is the older wording; the one at the head is the "Read with #2557's answers…" text. Regenerate the block (e.g. `pkit pm edit-pr`) so the person sees the answers as they stand at the head.
- [advisory] (pre-existing: `framing.py` is untouched, and the change makes no claim about its messages) Producer messages there still say "seam 1". outputs.md now says the seam is 2, and that producers are handed what version 1 had. The wording is not false, but the follow-up the PR body suggests is worth filing.
- [advisory] outputs.md, Previews: "The declaration names every primitive and property a scene of format 1 holds" is still true: `svg_declaration.py` now names `paragraphs` and `lines`, and per-run properties sit inside them. It could say "at seam 2" to tie the claim to the new run properties.
- **The four `updated` pages:** each matches its diff. Their sentences, apart from the checks.md one above, match what changed:
- **The scene example in components.md** matches what `scene.py` emits: `paragraphs`, per-run `style`/`fill`/`fonts`/`measured`/`sources`, and lines with `baseline`, `paragraph` and `spans`.
- **The README's "unchanged" reason holds:** the README names no seam version, scene property or finding that runs alter.
- **JRN-011's "unchanged" reason holds:** it needs only the library component in a new library version from UC-110, and the UC-110 edit leaves that as it was.
- **The UC-110 edit and the changeset** agree with DEC-012 and the code.

Reviewer agent (local, code-reviewer): APPROVED

- **One-run text is unchanged.** `break_runs` with a single run breaks lines, rstrips and measures widths as `_paragraph` did. In the SVG renderer, `_look` returns nothing for a run that looks like the first, so the line `<tspan>` stays the same. Contrast is measured at the same middle point, because the span's width equals the line's width. This matches the PR's claim that the pinned outputs did …
- **Run indices agree.** `Span.run` counts runs within a paragraph after empty parts are dropped. The scene's `paragraphs` and the renderer's `runs[span["run"]]` count the same way.
- **No partial runs reach the scene.** If a role fails partway through `_build_text`, the node is marked not present, and `texts()` skips it. So `compute_scene` never sees a half-filled text, and `max(node.runs, …)` in `_text` cannot run on an empty list.
- **Duplicate findings are filtered.** The renderer calls `_paint` once per span and the scene calls `paint` once per run. Repeated losses and `no-colour` findings are deduplicated (`_lose`, `Context.add`).
- **Paths match.** The run-list paths that `_lists` skips are built with `_item`, the same way `_Fields` builds them.
- [advisory] `checks.py`, `_Locked._read` copies the logic `pipeline.py` uses to find a component's file (around line 473), with one difference: it parses the lock's version with `Version.parse` where the pipeline uses the string as written. The two copies can drift. If they disagree, `id_findings` checks a run list as a list of items. Today that is harmless, because runs carry no `id`. Reusing th …
- [advisory] `scene.py`, `_run`: when a run's text holds a line feed, the run appears in several paragraphs. Each appearance lists `fonts` from the whole run's text, so a paragraph can name a font none of its own characters use. In the SVG this only adds an empty `@font-face` entry; the font subsets are still built per span. It is over-inclusive, not wrong.
- [advisory] `checks.py`, `_text_contrast`: if any one span of a text lies over a picture, the whole text goes unmeasured, including runs over plain fills. This keeps the old whole-text rule, so a reviewer still judges the case, but a mixed run over a box is now left out too.

- [advisory] **Run text in the SVG output is escaped.** In `plugins/svg.py`, `_Canvas` text drawing, each span's text passes through `escape(..., quote=False)` before it goes into element content. Each new `<tspan>` attribute (`font-family`, `font-size`, `font-weight`, `fill`, `fill-opacity`) goes through `_attribute`, which escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and `"`. Family names also go through `css_string`. …
- [advisory] **The new component reader in `checks.py` (`_Locked._read`) cannot be steered outside the piece.** It builds a file path from a content-supplied `use` and from the lock's version. `names.split_use` accepts each part only if `is_name` passes (lower-case words, so no `/`, no `..`), and the version must parse with `Version.parse`. Missing files and files that fail to read are treated as …
- [advisory] (pre-existing: the diff does not change it, and the PR makes no claim about it) `escape()` does not remove control characters that XML 1.0 forbids in text content. A run whose text contains such a character would make the SVG malformed. Span text has the same exposure that line text had before this change. This is a robustness issue rather than an exploitable hole. It could be hardene …

Reviewer agent (local, code-reviewer): APPROVED

- [advisory] `scene.py` `_text` and `layout.py` `Instance.unpainted`: a run whose concept fails to resolve gets two findings. `_run_concept` already reports `unknown-concept` at the run and returns None. If the run's style is painted with a role, `unpainted` still says the concept "shows in no colour", which adds a second finding for the same run. Having `unpainted` skip runs whose concept did not …
- [advisory] `checks.py` `_Fields._value`: a field marked `x-pkit-runs` whose mark is malformed (`run_problem` is not None) and that holds a list falls through to `runs-unmarked`. That message says "only a field its component marks `x-pkit-runs` takes a list of runs", but the field is marked. The component's `component-shape` finding names the real cause, so this only makes the content finding mis …
- [advisory] `scene.py` `_run`: `instance.paint(part.name, "fill", run)` runs once per run inside `ctx.attempt`. A text of many runs whose paint fails, such as a family with no matching member, may record the same `no-colour` fault once per run, unless `ctx` removes duplicates. Similarly, svg.py `_look` calls `_paint` once per span, so a missing colour can produce one loss per span.
- [advisory] `checks.py` `id_findings`: it now builds a `_Fields` reader just to learn which lists hold runs, and passes it a findings list that is then thrown away. That is fine for now. If `_Fields` later gets side effects beyond `found`, this second read of the content could become surprising, so a comment there, or a separate "which paths hold runs" pass, would make the intent clearer.
- [advisory] `layout.py` `_marks_below` and `_refs` only follow `items` and `properties`. A mark or `$ref` under another composition keyword, such as `anyOf` or `additionalProperties`, is not caught. That matches the "fixed subset" the `_Fields` docstring states, so it is not a defect, but the check is only as strict as that subset.

- [advisory] **The SVG renderer's new `<tspan>` runs are escaped correctly** (`plugins/svg.py`, `_text` / `_look`). This is the change's main injection surface: content text and brand-supplied font and paint values are now written into per-run `<tspan>`s.
- [advisory] **The new component reading cannot be used for path traversal** (`checks.py`, `_read`). It builds a file path from a `use` value, but `names.split_use` only accepts lower-case name segments, and the library version is parsed through `Version.parse`. A crafted `use` therefore can't escape the components folder. YAML is still read through the existing `read_yaml` / `load_yaml` helpers, …
- [advisory] Font embedding now covers every font a run draws in. The `@font-face` sources are still resolved by the existing `font_file` callable from the brand's families, and the change adds no file-system input of its own.
